clue.text: Pleasure is fantastic, possibly embracing love

indicators.note: embracing means the rearranged letters hug the next piece inside them
'possibly' suggests the words before it could be arranged some other way

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone declares that pleasure is wonderful, especially when love is part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' reads as praise for pleasure, but it is fodder; 'possibly' makes SATISFACTIN, and 'embracing' puts O inside before the final N.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the contentment of getting what you wanted is pleasure.

clue.text: Hone small instrument tip, interminably …

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a harp is a stringed musical instrument

indicators.note: interminably, without an end, tells us to drop the last letter of the word for tip

parts.note: the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: Instructions for sharpening the point of a small instrument, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' cuts the final D from END, leaving EN. The ellipsis joins this clue to 2 Down in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hone a blade is to make its edge keener.

clue.text: … narrow to acute point, end reduced originally

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the words just before it

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 Down: the instrument should be narrowed to a sharp point, with its end made smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue describes the answer too, so it reads almost as a whole-clue definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to taper is to become gradually thinner towards one end.

clue.text: In dissent I'm entitled to opinion

indicators.note: In says the answer sits within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A dissenter insists they have a right to their own view.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a view or feeling held about something is an opinion.

clue.text: First character with mother? No

parts.note: the first character of the alphabet is the letter A
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A riddle: who was the first person, and did he have a mother?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the first man in Genesis was made, not born, so he had no mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical reference: the first human created in the Book of Genesis, who had no parents.

clue.text: Piece from Mozart, he's piano player

indicators.note: Piece from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pianist is described as playing a work by Mozart.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an actor, someone who plays parts on stage, is a player.

clue.text: Fantastic Loire providing room with a view

indicators.note: fantastic, wildly imaginative, says the river name's letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: The Loire valley is so splendid it gives a room a fine outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loire' wants to be scenery; it is only five letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a projecting bay window gives a small room an outward view.

clue.text: Noisy fellow supporting proposal

indicators.note: supporting, in a down clue, means the fellow goes underneath the proposal

parts.note: a plan is a proposal put forward
gent, short for gentleman, means a fellow

explanation.surface: A loud man backs a suggestion at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: a plangent sound is loud and resonant, often mournfully so.

clue.text: Some underwear shows outlines

definitions.meaning: close-fitting pants are a kind of underwear
summaries or instructions given to someone, as to a barrister

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: snug underpants, and short summaries of instructions.

clue.text: A soft extremity in leaf insect's leg perhaps

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: in places the word for extremity inside the word for leaf

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page
an end is an extremity

explanation.surface: A tender tip on a leaf insect's leg, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaf insect' reads as one creature, but 'leaf' is wordplay and 'insect's leg' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a limb or antenna attached to an insect's body is a projecting part.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing compiler had line with Queen

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, I, so 'compiler had' is I'D
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The setter admits to a line about a useless royal acquaintance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lazy layabout who does nothing useful.

clue.text: Consent for each male before sex

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
it is old slang for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: A rule that each man must agree before any intimacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to consent to something is to allow it.

clue.text: Wealth posh left in old money?

indicators.note: in places posh and left inside the word for money

parts.note: pence are coins, money
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Is wealth really just a fancy word for old coins?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: great riches and luxurious abundance are wealth.

clue.text: More agreeable pocketing a thousand pounds

indicators.note: pocketing means the agreeable word holds the thousand inside it

parts.note: nicer means more pleasant, more agreeable
K, kilo, stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone is in a better mood after pocketing a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicker is British slang for a pound sterling, unchanged in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: British informal word for pounds, as in fifty of them.

clue.text: Principal motor noise the French raised

parts.note: motor is an informal word for a car
a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the French word is read upwards

parts.note: la is French for the, feminine

explanation.surface: A main car noise lifted by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cardinal as an adjective means chief or of prime importance.

clue.text: Bunny Girl, say, with first-class tail

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with 1 read as I
a tress is a long lock of hair, like a ponytail

explanation.surface: A Playboy Bunny Girl with a fluffy tail on her costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Playboy Club Bunny Girls served drinks, so one is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Bunny Girls were costumed hostesses who served tables at Playboy clubs.

clue.text: Charged in tars' case then left in exile

indicators.note: in places the word for charged inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: to charge is to rush or run, so charged is ran
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor charged at sea, then sent away to a penal colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like the definition; it is RAN. The outside letters of tars' are T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical sense: convicts were sent overseas to penal colonies as punishment, a form of banishment.

clue.text: Company present and correct finally about new orderly

indicators.note: about means the earlier pieces go round the letter for new

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word correct

explanation.surface: A firm's staff all present and correct, in neat order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present and correct' reads as a stock phrase, but 'and' is just a joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: clear and logically arranged, as in a lucid, well-ordered argument.

clue.text: People circling grass by house briefly in race

indicators.note: circling means the word for people goes round the next pieces

parts.note: man means humankind, people in general
to grass, or rat, is to inform on someone
HO is the short form of house

explanation.surface: Spectators surround a lawn beside a house during a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long-distance running event of about twenty-six miles.

clue.text: Following motorway exhaust's hot inside creating accident

indicators.note: Following says the drained part comes after the road

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI

indicators.note: inside places hot within the word for exhaust

parts.note: to sap is to exhaust, and the 's stands for has
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A car exhaust overheating after a motorway journey causes a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unlucky mishandled event, a minor misfortune.

clue.text: Cases of retsina got among common people

indicators.note: cases of takes the outside letters of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Crates of Greek wine reached the ordinary folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a disorderly rabble, the riff-raff of a population.

clue.text: Deity moves around divine saint

indicators.note: around means the word for moves goes round the divine

parts.note: goes means moves
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a divine

explanation.surface: A god travels around a holy saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective linked to Deity; it is a noun for a clergyman, DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a female god is a deity.

clue.text: Single female priest's upset about nuns' leader

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the nuns' leader
upset means knocked over, so the priest's letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters of priests, taking the 's as an S

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of nuns'

explanation.surface: A priest is troubled by the head of a convent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles PRIESTS into SPISTER, and 'about' wraps it round the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated term: an unmarried woman, especially an older one.

clue.text: Outburst of universal vociferation

indicators.note: of signals that the answer comes out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A burst of shouting from everyone at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a sudden volley, like a burst of applause or criticism.

clue.text: Jersey, perhaps, one's left with

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S
and means with, together

explanation.surface: Someone is left holding only a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, off France.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Jersey is a Channel Island, so a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Don Quixote's sidekick?

parts.note: Sancho Panza was his companion, and a Spanish speaker would call such a companion a friend in Spanish

explanation.walkthrough: Don Quixote is Spanish, so his companion would be called by the Spanish word for friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish word for a friend or pal, apt for a Spanish knight's companion.

clue.text: Spirit raised showing destiny

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the word for spirit reads upwards

parts.note: mood means frame of mind, spirit

explanation.surface: A lifted spirit reveals what fate holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unhappy fate, a grim destiny.

clue.text: Draw on a screen for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means the words are spoken to listeners

parts.note: a veil is a screen that hides something

explanation.surface: Drawing a veil across a screen in front of the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw on a screen' suggests drawing pictures; 'Draw on' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to avail yourself of something is to make use of it.

clue.text: Save someone with ice almost melting

indicators.note: melting suggests the letters losing their form and rearranging
almost means the last letter of ice is dropped

explanation.surface: Cut costs by rescuing someone trapped in ice that is thawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ICE to IC; 'melting' shuffles SOMEONE plus IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cut back on spending in order to put money aside.

clue.text: Put on costume, turning arrogant

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters revolving into a new order

explanation.surface: Dressing up makes someone haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: scornful and looking down on others, haughty.
